# everpure_azure_create_platform_console_ssh_user (Action)

Creates a user on the platform console of an existing Storage Pool and sets its SSH public key, so the user can log in to the console over SSH. Needs Terraform 1.14 or later, and 1.16 or later to refer to the triggering resource with `caller` in an `action_trigger`.

~> **This action can be run only once per user.** It creates a new user, and any later run for the same `username` fails with a 409 "already exists" error. That includes users that were not created by this action, such as users created in the platform console and its built-in users. Changing or removing the configuration does not change or remove a user that already exists. To set an SSH key for an existing user, or to change a user's keys or role, use the platform console's GUI or REST API.

Logging in to the platform console as the user this action creates and logging in with temporary credentials are independent ways in; use either or both. For the temporary credentials, see the `everpure_azure_platform_console_activation_credentials` ephemeral resource.

The Storage Pool must have the platform console enabled.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Create a platform console user on demand.
#
# Nothing here runs automatically. Create the user with:
#
#   terraform apply -invoke=action.everpure_azure_create_platform_console_ssh_user.admin
#
# The action only creates new users: it fails if the user already exists. Requires
# Terraform 1.14 or later.

terraform {
  required_providers {
    everpure = {
      source = "PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure"
    }
  }
}

provider "everpure" {
  subscription_id = var.subscription_id
}

variable "subscription_id" {
  type = string
}

variable "console_public_key_path" {
  type    = string
  default = "~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub"
}

data "everpure_azure_storage_pool" "example" {
  name                = "pool-prod-east"
  resource_group_name = "rg-storage-prod"
}

action "everpure_azure_create_platform_console_ssh_user" "admin" {
  config {
    storage_pool_id = data.everpure_azure_storage_pool.example.id
    username        = "tfadmin"
    role            = "array_admin"
    public_key      = file(var.console_public_key_path)
  }
}

# To give the user several keys, put one per line, for example with
# join("\n", [file("a.pub"), file("b.pub")]), or point public_key at a whole
# authorized_keys file.
```

```terraform
# Create a platform console user right after the Storage Pool is created.
#
# The action runs once, when the pool is created. In-place updates of the pool do not
# run it again, changing the key or role here later does nothing, and replacing the
# pool creates the user on the new pool. To change a user afterwards, use the platform
# console's GUI or REST API.
#
# Requires Terraform 1.16 or later: `caller` refers to the resource that triggered the
# action, which avoids a dependency cycle between the pool and the action.

terraform {
  required_providers {
    everpure = {
      source = "PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure"
    }
  }
}

provider "everpure" {
  subscription_id = var.subscription_id
}

variable "subscription_id" {
  type = string
}

variable "reservation_id" {
  type = string
}

variable "subnet_id" {
  type = string
}

variable "console_public_key_path" {
  type    = string
  default = "~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub"
}

action "everpure_azure_create_platform_console_ssh_user" "admin" {
  config {
    storage_pool_id = caller.id
    username        = "tfadmin"
    role            = "array_admin"
    public_key      = file(var.console_public_key_path)
  }
}

resource "everpure_azure_storage_pool" "this" {
  name                          = "pool-prod-east"
  resource_group_name           = "rg-storage-prod"
  location                      = "eastus2"
  zone                          = "1"
  reservation_id                = var.reservation_id
  provisioned_bandwidth_in_mbps = 1024

  vnet_injection {
    subnet_id = var.subnet_id
  }

  platform_console {
    gui_enabled = true
    api_enabled = true
    cli_enabled = true
  }

  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_create]
      actions = [action.everpure_azure_create_platform_console_ssh_user.admin]
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- action schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `public_key` (String) SSH public key of the user, in OpenSSH one-line format (`<type> <base64 key> [comment]`). To give the user several keys, put one per line. The value is sent to the service unchanged, so `file()` of a `.pub` file or of an `authorized_keys` file works. The provider only rejects values that are plainly not public keys: empty values, private keys and PEM blocks, and lines without both a key type and key data. The service decides which key types it accepts.
- `role` (String) Role the user gets on the platform console: `array_admin` (full administrative access) or `read_only`. There is no default, so that administrative access is never granted implicitly.
- `storage_pool_id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the Storage Pool. Must be in the provider's own `subscription_id`.
- `username` (String) Name of the user to create. Must not already exist on the Storage Pool; the service rejects an empty name and any name already in use.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `invoke` (String) Defaults to 5 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when creating the user.
